races.name: Aalberts Ips Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's stable is in form (6/88 past 14 days) and this horse has placed at 6f on Good recently, but its natural hold-up style is doubly problematic here — genuinely running against the race shape over a flat 6f with one front-runner, and squeezed further back than its best position by the redistribution dynamic; the style fit discount is merited.

runners_data.name: Triple P
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in the field and, with a Good to Firm surface reading fast and Doncaster's straight 6f suiting a horse able to bowl along unchallenged, the tactical position here is as good as it gets; Jake Dickson (5lb claim) keeps the weight low and last run 13 days ago suggests sharpness.

runners_data.name: Spruces Due
runners_data.note: Headgear (h) could sharpen focus on this 48-day absence, but a hold-up profile over 6f against an unhurried pace is structurally difficult; the best form came over 7f on Standard, and the drop to 6f on Good to Firm for M Mullineaux's yard (0/2 past 14 days) adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Sakura Impact
runners_data.note: Third on debut over 8f on Good for Mrs I G-Leveque (0/2 past 14 days) showed promise but the step down to 6f is a significant trip reduction; a hold-up style is workable if the pace is genuine, making Scenario B the most relevant opening for this horse, though 24 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners a horse with a consistent prominent style and recent placed form at 6f on Good (2nd at Carlisle); the hood is fitted and the 12-day turnaround suggests fitness — this is the only horse likely to push up to Triple P and influence the race shape from early on.

runners_data.name: Kohana Nation
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes the ride for Charles Hills (2/19 past 14 days) on a lightly raced three-year-old returning after 225 days, with running style unknown and both previous starts over 7f on Standard; the unknown tactical profile and extended layoff make assessment very difficult, though Charles Hills can place horses fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Triple P is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, should be able to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from stall to home on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster. Brash is the only other genuinely prominent type and will look to sit just off Triple P's shoulder, meaning the pace is real but not a war — a steady-to-moderate early tempo is the most probable outcome. The hold-up contingent of Stoneacre Joe, Spruces Due, and Sakura Impact will be anchored in the rear half, with Kohana Nation's style unknown adding a further variable in the closing stages. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner over a flat 6f on fast ground — clearly favours horses with the tactical speed to race prominently and quicken from the front or close proximity, making the lead-to-prominent profile the dominant winning profile. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically run into contention from the back; Stoneacre Joe carries a redistribution tag and is unlikely to secure a position that suits, further concentrating advantage on the pace-end of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Triple P Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Triple P bowls into an uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout, Brash unable to apply meaningful pressure.
scenarios.body: Triple P settles into a relaxed rhythm at the head of affairs and, with Good to Firm ground riding quick and no challenger forcing the pace, has energy reserves to quicken inside the final furlong; front-runners are structurally advantaged here given the lack of pace rivals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Produces Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Brash pushes up aggressively to challenge Triple P's lead, turning the opening furlongs into a genuine battle.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace on quick ground burns off the leaders sooner than expected, allowing a horse sitting just off the speed in third or fourth to pick up the pieces; Brash's previous placed form at 6f gives it the fitness and experience to survive a contested race better than most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is faster than expected and the front two tire inside the final two furlongs, opening a lane for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Sakura Impact or Spruces Due, tracking midfield, produce a sustained finish on the faster surface; however, this scenario is discounted because Stoneacre Joe — the most natural hold-up type — is mapped out of role and the true rear-runners face a structurally difficult task over 6f at Doncaster with a modest pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Kohana Nation, unknown in style and returning from 225 days off, produces a performance significantly above market expectation.
scenarios.body: A Charles Hills-trained three-year-old with an unknown tactical profile could slot anywhere in the field and produce an eye-catching run on reappearance; the long layoff and limited form (two starts, best of 2nd) make this a low-probability swing.

watchPoints.text: Watch Triple P in the opening two furlongs — if it bowls clear unchallenged and settles quickly on Good to Firm ground, the race may effectively be over before halfway; any horse positioned more than four lengths off the leader at the 3f mark faces a very steep task.

Brash's early intentions are critical — if David Nolan pushes for a prominent position and ends up in a closer battle with Triple P than expected, the pace dynamic shifts materially and hold-up horses suddenly become relevant.

Kohana Nation's unknown running style after a 225-day absence is a genuine variable; if Oisin Orr elects to race prominently rather than hold up, the front end becomes more congested than the map suggests.

Stoneacre Joe's redistribution tag means connections will struggle to get it into a position that suits — watch at the start to see whether Harry Russell attempts to push forward early, which would signal a change of tactics and slightly upgrade its chances.

Going is reported as Good to Firm throughout the card — faster than the race-day going of Good stated in the race header — so horses with a preference for quicker ground (particularly those on the pace) may receive an unexpected boost.

races.name: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Encounter
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form at 7f on Good going (three runs, all placed at this trip), but the STYLE_FIT flag indicates she is racing out of her most natural role here, so her market position should be tempered slightly — her front-running in a race mapped as prominent is workable but not ideal if a rival forces her wider than expected.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts either side of a sixth last time out give Encounter a solid recent profile, and he has run over today's trip before; drawn three carrying 135 lb, the main risk is that he's yet to win in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Weleyff
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Good ground last time and has a clean 2/2 similar-going record — Edward Bethell's 2/25 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's own form profile is the most convincing in the field, with a win and a place suggesting she handles this trip and surface with authority.
runners_data.comment: Weleyff arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, with our rating of 86 marking him out as a leading threat from stall 4; the main risk is whether a third placing two starts back hints at vulnerability under 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Eighth Immortal
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced two-year-old with unknown style mapping, who has placed at both 6f and 7f on Good ground — the step up in experience is the key variable, and Jack Jones' 0/17 14-day record gives no trainer confidence angle, meaning the horse's raw form must do the talking.
runners_data.comment: Eighth Immortal arrives here in good heart after consecutive placed efforts — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back — with experience over today's trip and a rating of 96 to underpin his claims; winless in recent starts, but the form holds up well.

runners_data.name: Lincoln Warrior
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh takes the ride on this hold-up type whose best placing (2nd at 6f on Standard) came on a different surface, and whose three similar-going runs have produced just 0 wins and 0 places — Ivan Furtado's 4/23 14-day rate offers some optimism but the form profile is simply too thin to suggest he can win from off the pace here.
runners_data.comment: Lincoln Warrior shaped with promise when second two starts back, and has run over today's trip — the main concern is he's yet to win in recent starts, though at 128 lb from stall 5, connections will be hoping that placed effort translates into something more.

runners_data.name: Prince Kameo
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's record with laid-off horses demands respect, but 53 days between runs combined with a "fades in finish" flag, the lowest OR in the field at 66, and a 1/3 similar-going record make this a tough assignment — the 7f trip is also a step beyond his best efforts, which have all come at 6f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Prince Kameo faces a stiff task here; 53 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and a draw of two at least gives him a position to work from.

races.paceDynamic: Encounter is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 7f nursery on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster, and with no other horse rated as a natural leader, she is set to control proceedings from the outset at a sustainable, uncontested tempo. Weleyff will press from a prominent position, but the pace is unlikely to be searingly fast — Doncaster's straight seven is unforgiving at slow-to-moderate fractions, and a controlled gallop typically compresses the field rather than stringing it out. Lincoln Warrior and Prince Kameo sit at the back as hold-up types, but both carry modest form and significant concerns — Prince Kameo fades in the finish and Lincoln Warrior has no win or placing from similar conditions. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs rather than a short, late burst — the prominent-racing profile holds the commanding tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Encounter Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Encounter dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop from the front, inviting no serious challenge until the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Encounter and Weleyff, both positioned at or near the head of affairs, are best placed to exploit a compressed, front-dominated race on this flat, straight track where position is rarely surrendered late. A controlled pace suits those with stamina and track position over pure finishing speed, making prominent racers the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Eighth Immortal Emerges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the lightly-raced Eighth Immortal, stepping up in distance, produces a sustained finish to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: Eighth Immortal has shown progressive form placing at both 6f and 7f on Good ground and is unknown enough to be dangerous in a small field if fitness levels are right. The unknown style tag adds uncertainty, but the 7f trip and similar-going record make this more than speculative.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a surprisingly brisk pace is set and Lincoln Warrior or Prince Kameo close from off the pace in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lincoln Warrior's best efforts have come over 6f and he has never won or placed in conditions this similar, while Prince Kameo fades late and has poor similar-going form — both face uphill tasks even if the shape briefly plays into their hands. This scenario requires a pace scenario that simply does not look likely given the lone front-runner setting a manageable tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses underperform and a rank outsider benefits from chaos or an unusually strong pace that collapses the field.
scenarios.body: Prince Kameo, trained by the high-strike-rate Sir Mark Prescott, carries fitness questions after 53 days off and has the worst similar-going record in the field, making this a long-shot scenario dependent on exceptional circumstances rather than form logic. This shape would require almost every favourite narrative to fail simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Weleyff's 7f Good-ground win last time gives her the standout profile in this race — watch whether Oisin Orr positions her prominently from the off to press Encounter and take advantage of the uncontested pace.

Prince Kameo carries a "fades in finish" flag and is 53 days off — watch for any signs of greenness or slow away from the stalls that could confirm the hold-up style concern is compounding his stamina limitations.

Eighth Immortal is lightly raced with an unknown tactical style — watch where Ryan Sexton places him in the opening furlong, as any prominent positioning could make him a material danger if the pace stays sustainable.

Encounter's trainer S Woods holds a 0/11 14-day record — while that is not determinative, if she fades in the final furlong after controlling the race, it is consistent with a yard not currently firing at its best.

With only five runners and a single confirmed pace-setter, monitor whether the race develops an unusually slow early gallop — if fractions are slack, the final two furlongs at Doncaster will become a sprint test that flatters those with the highest top speed rather than those who stay prominently.

races.name: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Yates Drywall Ltd Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mariner
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice in good-ground conditions at 8f and brings a 9-day fresh turnaround for Jennie Candlish; the step up to 1m2f is a query given all his similar-going form is over 8f, but tracking Super Hit from a handy position plays to his strengths and Jude Fernandes claims 7lb.
runners_data.comment: Mariner finished third two starts back and followed up with fourth last time, and with experience over today's trip and going, he makes appeal at a handy weight of 132 lb from stall three, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Magic Runner
runners_data.note: 127-day absence is a significant concern for this hold-up type, and all recent starts were on Southwell's all-weather surface rather than turf, making the switch back to good to firm ground at Doncaster a genuine unknown; needs the pace to be strong enough to close from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Magic Runner landed a win earlier in this sequence and has built experience over today's trip and conditions, carrying 128 lb from stall four; the worry is she arrives 127 days between runs and her last two outings have been unplaced.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who shaped as a hold-up horse earlier in his career but has won twice leading from the front on good ground over 10f; with no rival to press him he should find a comfortable rhythm, though the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 reflects that this is not his most natural role and his chance is sensitive to whether he is headed mid-race.
runners_data.comment: Super Hit arrives on the back of a win last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and is trained by a yard firing at 36% — the main question is whether 137 lb blunts his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up performer who reverts to a headgear-free run and arrives 16 days fresh; his similar-going record is thin (1 win from 11 equivalent starts) and he has been out of the frame in three successive good-ground runs, suggesting the fast surface and the lack of a truly strong pace work against him.
runners_data.comment: Cosmos Raj arrives here in good order just 16 days after his last start, has experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating just edges him to the top of these — yet the stark reality is he's winless in his last five starts, and finding a way to convert that promise into a finish is the pressing concern.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Pete
runners_data.note: Consistent back-marker who has finished 6th, 9th, 11th and 13th in recent turf starts on good ground, with zero wins in similar conditions; the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects that genuine rear-of-field positions are over-subscribed in this field, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers expectations even if he finds his preferred spot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with four unplaced efforts among them, Whiskey Pete is hard to fancy despite carrying 125 lb from stall 5 with a run nine days ago under his belt; he has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 60 offers a slim crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Steps In Time
runners_data.note: Recent form includes a hurdles campaign (17f, 16f starts) before returning to flat action over 10f; while naturally a hold-up type, the fact this race lacks the pace he would need to close on means he is shown in midfield and his 0.90 style-fit discount is warranted — Philip Kirby's stable has had no winners in the last 11 runners, adding a trainer angle worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a ninth last time out and an unseated rider two back, Steps In Time is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 124 lb from stall two and having run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Super Hit is the confirmed front runner here and, with no other natural pace-setter to challenge, should secure a comfortable lead into the long Doncaster straight and control tempo on good to firm ground. Mariner will press from a prominent position, but with the pace uncontested Super Hit can dictate a sustainable, measured gallop that shapes this as a race run to suit those tracking the leader rather than deep closers. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Whiskey Pete and Steps In Time are natural back-of-the-field horses redistributed to midfield because Cosmos Raj and Magic Runner also want to come from off the pace, leaving rear-end positions genuinely congested. A controlled, single-paced gallop on a flat, fast-ground track with one unchallenged front runner gives the clearest advantage to a prominent or tracking runner who can maintain rhythm and pounce in the straight without needing a wall of pace to run into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Super Hit Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit leads from the front without pressure and sets a measured, even tempo throughout the 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Super Hit controls the race from the front, keeping the gallop honest but not excessive, and the rail-hugging Doncaster straight rewards the horse who has been travelling economically in the slipstream; Mariner, tracking prominently, is ideally placed to challenge in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit sets a slightly stronger pace than expected and a prominent tracking horse gets a perfect draught before asserting.
scenarios.body: The even Doncaster straight becomes a two-furlong sprint for the horse who has covered every move, and a front two or three become exposed; Mariner's course profile at this trip and going suits this outcome, with Cosmos Raj capable of getting into contention if the pace lifts sufficiently to bring the hold-up runners into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fastest
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and create meaningful ground for genuine closers to make up.
scenarios.body: Cosmos Raj or Magic Runner would need the gallop to be genuinely taxing to reel in Super Hit from off the pace on flat Doncaster ground, and with the redistributed hold-up horses Whiskey Pete and Steps In Time likely unable to reach their natural rear position, the true late finish is a narrower proposition than it appears on paper.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit falters or is pulled up mid-race and the tempo drops to a crawl, triggering a sprint finish from midfield.
scenarios.body: A truly falsely-run race on fast ground would compress the field and theoretically suit Whiskey Pete or Steps In Time, but both are racing out of their natural role and carry style-fit discounts that undermine their winning prospects even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Super Hit — if anything challenges him for the lead in the first two furlongs, the unchallenged pace dynamic collapses and the dominant scenario probability drops sharply; watch the early stages closely for any pressure from Mariner pushing forward.

Magic Runner — 127 days off and a switch from all-weather to good to firm turf is a combination that could see this horse flat to the boards in the straight; watch for early signs of reluctance or sluggishness from James Sullivan leaving the gate.

Whiskey Pete and Steps In Time — both are natural hold-up horses occupying congested rear positions; if they are locked wide or unable to settle, neither is in a position to land their best effort and the late-finishing scenario becomes even less credible.

Cosmos Raj — a headgear-free run for this eight-year-old is worth tracking; if David Nolan keeps him closer than his recent form suggests, it could indicate the horse is well-treated under OR=65 and the trainer has spotted a pace setup he wants to exploit.

races.name: Winners Wear Skopes Menswear Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Haaderr
runners_data.note: Solo pace-setter with strong recent form (1-2-2 in last three on similar going), handled Good ground well in three of four runs; Edward Bethell yard in fair recent form and Oisin Orr provides a stable booking — the lone front-runner on a flat straight track on Good to Firm is a significant positional asset.
runners_data.comment: Haaderr arrives here in good heart — a winner two starts back and runner-up in two of his last four, with experience over today's trip and conditions — but his fourth last time out is the flag to watch.

runners_data.name: Suspicious Mindz
runners_data.note: Won a 6f Good ground handicap last time out and steps up to 7f here; the Shay Farmer (5lb claim) booking is notable, and six runs on Good or Good to Firm ground show a consistent prominent style that should sit just off Haaderr — best-placed of the genuine pressure horses in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Suspicious Mindz arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while 134 lb from stall 2 is the factor to weigh; that seventh the start before is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: First Time
runners_data.note: Has placed in four of his last five on Good-type ground and the Fahey yard is in fair form, but a genuine front-runner by inclination who is denied his natural spot by the depth of prominent runners; racing in a role that is somewhat alien to him means his chance depends on finding a clean passage from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in his last two starts and runner-up five starts back, First Time brings solid recent consistency to this contest; he has run over today's trip and going before, and his rating of 92 heads the field, though the trainer's current 2% strike rate is a minor note of caution.

runners_data.name: Vidmiyr
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's yard has had a productive fortnight (5/22 T14), and Vidmiyr won a 7f Good ground handicap earlier this season, giving him solid course-and-distance credentials; by nature a prominent racer, he finds himself pushed further back than he would like and will need traffic to clear earlier than the flat Doncaster straight typically allows.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and unplaced last time, Vidmiyr makes the shortlist hard work despite being placed in five of his six recent runs and having experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Goldwork
runners_data.note: Wears tongue tie and blinkers and is fresh off a 7-day turnaround, which Eve Johnson Houghton sometimes does with purpose; predominantly a 6f horse stepping back up to 7f with modest placed form at the trip, and as a true hold-up type he needs a stronger-than-expected pace to deliver his late effort.
runners_data.comment: Goldwork has placed third twice in his last three starts, showing admirable consistency at this level, and has run over today's trip and going — the main concern is that he's yet to win in recent starts and must prove he can convert placed efforts into something more.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: 59 days since last run is a concern and his recent form over 5f and 6f on softer ground contrasts with today's 7f Good to Firm conditions — stepping up in trip to a track and surface combination he has yet to show affinity for makes him the most speculative of the hold-up brigade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Shadow Run has at least run over today's trip before and carries a manageable 122 lb from stall four, but a 59-day absence and an unplaced latest effort make him hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Haaderr is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to dispute the lead on the Good to Firm ground over this flat Doncaster 7f, he should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the outset. Suspicious Mindz will press from a prominent position, but with First Time and Vidmiyr both natural prominent types pushed back into midfield by sheer congestion, the pace picture ahead of them is unlikely to be truly strong. Goldwork and Shadow Run sit in the hold-up berths but have modest recent form figures and limited experience at this trip, narrowing their finishing kick. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, sustainable pace set by Haaderr on quick ground over a flat straight mile benefits horses who can race prominently and pick off a steady gallop in the final two furlongs — the prominent-to-midfield profile is best placed, provided they can recover their natural position. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can comfortably accommodate; Haaderr is most likely to actually lead, with Suspicious Mindz best-placed to hold a genuine pressing role ahead of the displaced First Time and Vidmiyr.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Haaderr Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Haaderr leads at a fair but unforced tempo on Good to Firm ground and none of the prominent runners can bridge the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Haaderr dictates from the front on ground he handles, building a lead that is never seriously threatened on the flat Doncaster straight; Suspicious Mindz, tracking closely, is the main danger but may find Haaderr's advantage too great if the pace is metered correctly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough on Good to Firm ground to string the field out and leave Haaderr vulnerable to a sustained challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Suspicious Mindz or one of the displaced prominent types — most likely First Time — gets competitive ground and dashes past a tying leader late; this shape suits horses who sit within two lengths of the pace and travel comfortably.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front end ties up late, creating a gap for the hold-up horses to exploit.
scenarios.body: Goldwork or Shadow Run, settled well off the pace, finds a run down the straight as the leaders come back to them; this scenario is less likely given neither is a true hold-up horse by form and the pace is expected to be modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If First Time or Vidmiyr push aggressively for position early and force Haaderr into a faster-than-ideal pace, scrambling the race shape.
scenarios.body: An overcrowded early battle for the prominent positions burns up the front half of the field, opening the door for a surprise result from the back; this is the least likely shape given Haaderr's style edge and the redistributed runners' out-of-role constraints.

watchPoints.text: Haaderr's early positioning is critical — if he jumps cleanly and establishes his lead within the first furlong unopposed, the race is likely over as a contest for the front-runners and prominent types cannot reclaim their natural spots.

First Time and Vidmiyr both pressing for the same prominent ground from the stalls could cause early crowding on the near-side rail, disrupting the race shape for multiple runners in the first two furlongs.

Goldwork's short 7-day turnaround combined with tongue tie and blinkers headgear suggests connections may have a specific target in mind — watch for market moves if this stable angle sharpens pre-race.

Shadow Run's 59-day absence and untested profile at 7f on Good to Firm makes him difficult to assess; monitor his pre-race behaviour and market as a guide to whether connections believe the step up in trip will unlock improvement.

The Good to Firm going report is consistent across all Doncaster races today, confirming fast conditions that will favour a fluent galloper with a clean action — any horse flagged with a going concern on this surface should be discounted accordingly.

races.name: Harrison College Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lass
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly with a strong sim-going record (10/15, 3 wins, 4 placed) on good ground and a productive 1W run over today's 7f trip; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a real asset, and 28 days since last run keeps her fresh — the main danger from the back if she gets a clear run late.
runners_data.comment: Moonhall Lass won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, while a trainer firing at 36% adds stable confidence; however, she was only fourth last time out and her speed rating of 58 leaves something to prove at this level.

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's sprinter has been firing in six-furlong handicaps and races out of role at 7f for a hold-up type; naturally belongs at the rear but the packed hold-up field means she's likely to find herself racing closer than ideal — her 9/14 sim-going record suggests the conditions suit, but the extra furlong and positional compromise are genuine concerns.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and placed twice in his last five starts, Get Up Everybody arrives here fit on a 14-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on; winless in recent starts, but the top-rated runner on an official mark of 58 with more in hand than that suggests.

runners_data.name: Operation Gimcrack
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter and race-shaper: Bryan Smart's six-year-old has won over this exact course and distance and sets the tempo for the entire field; with no pressure forecast, his style-fit score reflects that he may be racing ahead of his true role, but being unopposed at the front is a significant tactical advantage today.
runners_data.comment: Has run over today's trip and going, and he showed winning form earlier in this sequence, but a sixth and an unplaced run in his last two starts are harder to ignore; 43 days off and 135 lb from stall 11 add further questions.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old is a confirmed hold-up type fitted with a tongue-strap, though forced into a midfield position given the volume of closers — his form figures over 7f at Good are uninspiring (760787) and the redistribution out of his natural comfort zone further tempers confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Rated 68 by us against an official mark of 56, Arnaz is winless in recent starts but that ratings gap suggests he's considerably better than his current mark; he has run over today's trip and going, and 32 days off should have him fresh — the risk is his recent finishes make confidence hard to sustain.

runners_data.name: Queensmaite
runners_data.note: S R Bowring's mare returns from a 95-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field and is a significant flag; her sim-going record is sparse (2 from 6) and she's never placed in this class, meaning the positional compromise as a redistributed hold-up type compounds an already difficult task on reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a ninth last time out and a seventh three starts back, Queensmaite also returns after a 95-day absence; experience over today's trip and going is the sole positive to cling to.

runners_data.name: Danrana
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with just three career runs and a ⚠ finish-fade flag, which is concerning in a race where closing late is the primary mode for most rivals; Fionn McSharry's stable has had only one runner in 14 days, and the 63-day absence adds further uncertainty about readiness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Danrana has been off 63 days and faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall three at least gives her a clean break.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Pink
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls' three-year-old has a solid similar-going record (7/12, 1 win, 4 placed) and has been raised to headgear (p) to sharpen focus; 14 days since her last run means she arrives fit, and she's a natural hold-up type who at least has the form profile to be competitive if the closing positions work out.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old has registered consecutive second-place finishes (2-2) over 7f on good ground and is well-exposed in this class; he holds up naturally but has been moved forward on the map — his recent placed consistency makes him one of the more interesting hold-up horses likely to secure a competitive position today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Emerald Army does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 16 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh; however, consecutive sixth-place finishes latest out and a rating of 53 make it hard to fancy him strongly from stall nine carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old holds a win at 6f on good ground and has a fine sim-going record (8/9), but steps up to 7f for the first time and today wears a tongue-tie for the first time too; holds up naturally yet is likely to press forward given the field dynamics — the trip and new headgear are unknowns but recent form (3-1-4 in last three) is strong.
runners_data.comment: Hares Bredth won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine danger at 129 lb from stall 2; the concern is that seventh last time out suggests he needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Liam Wright's 5lb claim is some compensation, but this three-year-old carries a ⚠ finish-fade flag and has a modest sim-going record (3/8); the visor goes on for the first time, a 58-day absence adds uncertainty, and being a redistributed hold-up type unable to get her natural position makes this a difficult puzzle to solve.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and yet to show the consistency to suggest a turnaround is imminent, Ryefield has at least run over today's trip and going before; carrying 126 lb from stall 10 after 58 days off, he looks a tough task at this level.

runners_data.name: Havana Oaks
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old has only one run on similar going (7th of 6f) and her form (55-67) shows no win or place; Joey Haynes takes the ride, but as the lowest-rated horse in the field (OR 52) pushed out of her natural closing position, she faces the steepest ask of any runner here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Havana Oaks faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and 26 days off should leave her fresh from stall one.

races.paceDynamic: Operation Gimcrack is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster. The straight, flat seven furlongs suits a horse who can dictate, and with no pressure expected through the early stages, Operation Gimcrack is likely to bowl along at a rhythm that keeps opponents honest without burning itself out. The field is packed with hold-up horses — Get Up Everybody, Arnaz, Hares Bredth, Emerald Army, Queensmaite, Havana Oaks and Ryefield are all natural hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because there is no room for all of them at the rear in a realistic race shape. Of those, Hares Bredth and Emerald Army are most likely to actually press forward from their draws and secure a more prominent position than their natural style suggests. This race shape — one honest pace-setter, a largely hold-up field unable to get its natural position — strongly favours the horse who can travel prominently behind the leader and produce a sustained finishing effort, rewarding the prominent-to-midfield profile rather than deep closers who will find little acceleration generated from a single front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Operation Gimcrack Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Operation Gimcrack bowls clear unchallenged and the hold-up horses fail to close on a flat, honest gallop.
scenarios.body: Operation Gimcrack sets its own fractions down the Doncaster straight with no rival willing to pressurise it, conserving enough energy to hold on; horses closest to the pace throughout — those who track from prominent or midfield — have the best chance of picking up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse who secures a prominent position tracks Operation Gimcrack closely and delivers a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: With a solo leader setting a moderate tempo, the horse that sits second or third and travels sweetly into the straight will have first run and enough gas to collar the leader; Hares Bredth's course-and-distance form and Emerald Army's recent 2nd-2nd sequence make them the most credible threats from this angle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Operation Gimcrack goes too fast early or ties up inside the final furlong and the genuine closers get a proper run through.
scenarios.body: A fast-finishing hold-up horse would need gaps to open in the straight and the tempo to have truly unravelled the leader; Sparkling Pink's 1W4P record in similar going and Moonhall Lass's placed record give them each a puncher's chance if the race plays into their hands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop causes the entire field to bunch in the straight, turning the finish into a sprint-finish scramble.
scenarios.body: With many hold-up horses unable to get to the rear, the field concertinas and it becomes a wall-to-wall dash in the final two furlongs where any position advantage is neutralised; Hares Bredth's strong recent sprint form and Sparkling Pink's consistency suit this chaotic finish best.

watchPoints.text: Operation Gimcrack is unchallenged in the lead — watch whether it dictates a crawl that allows the entire field to sprint past it late, or an honest gallop that sustains its advantage to the line.

Hares Bredth is going to a new trip (7f) and wearing a tongue-tie for the first time simultaneously — both represent genuine unknowns that could either unlock improvement or cause an unexpected backward step.

Queensmaite returns from 95 days off as a hold-up type forced out of her natural position; a flat reappearance from an undercooked mare in a race where position is already compromised could cost her early ground she never recovers.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Get Up Everybody, Arnaz, Emerald Army, Hares Bredth, Ryefield, Havana Oaks) all racing closer than ideal means early positional jostling in the first two furlongs could be significant — watch for crowding on the rail.

Sparkling Pink's recent headgear addition (p) combined with a 14-day turnaround and the best consistent placed record in similar going (7/12) makes her one to monitor through the early stages for any signs she's travelling more fluently than her odds suggest.

races.name: Harrison College Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Donald
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with form entirely over 5-6f and no win or place in seven attempts at 7f, making the trip a significant concern on Good to Firm; David Nolan takes the ride but sim-going stats (0W0P over 7f) do little to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Placed second five starts back, Donald has going experience to call on and arrives fit after 23 days, with our rating of 63 giving him a case as a live danger at stall three — the risk is he's been winless in his last five starts and that ninth last time out is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Wilde And Dandy
runners_data.note: Joey Haynes partners this Ivan Furtado-trained six-year-old who has placed three times in fifteen similar-ground starts and was third in his last two Sandown 7f runs — a genuine late runner who will be shuffled into a midfield berth he may not want given the hold-up congestion.
runners_data.comment: Wilde And Dandy shaped with promise when third two starts back and again five starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is in his favour; the main concern is that he's been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from a disappointing seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Groundsman
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane sends this four-year-old wearing a hood, and while he has placed at 7f on Tapeta it has been a wall of near-misses on turf; Oisin Orr takes the ride but his natural rear-of-field style is compromised by the crowded hold-up section, making a clear run genuinely uncertain.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Carries a warning flag for fading in finishes and has a patchy recent record — two wins at 7f but mostly mid-to-rear finishes — with Alex Jary (3lb claimer) unable to compensate for the fact this horse is being squeezed into a midfield slot rather than finding its preferred position off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of well-beaten efforts either side of a second two starts back, Sir David is hard to fancy against stronger rivals here; he has run over today's trip and going, and breaks from stall one.

runners_data.name: Barbuda Bay
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's three-year-old is returning after 49 days off and has a single placed effort from five similar-ground runs, while a fade-in-finish flag adds caution; Dougie Costello is an experienced partner but this horse's natural hold-up style is at odds with the limited opportunity to get a clear late run in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and a shade below her official mark on our rating, Barbuda Bay has experience over today's trip but has looked out of sorts recently; the 49-day break may have freshened her, though a pick-up in form is needed from stall nine carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's three-year-old has run well for place on Good going over 6f and Oliver Stammers keeps the ride; form figures show a second from eight attempts on similar ground and, while he hasn't won, he arrives just 14 days off his last run with a relatively compact frame that suits tracking close to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Von Trotter shaped well last time out, finishing second, and returns here on a quick 14-day turnaround in good order. He has run over today's trip before and, though winless in his last six starts, that recent placed effort suggests his confidence is intact heading into this.

runners_data.name: Sprinting Speed
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's three-year-old carries a fade-in-finish flag and has zero wins or places from seven Good-ground starts, with Stevie Donohoe unable to offset a profile that screams limited finishing thrust; 36 days since last run and a record of finishing mid-pack at best leaves this one vulnerable in a race where closing ground will be at a premium.
runners_data.comment: Ranked highest of the ten runners on ratings, Sprinting Speed has run over today's trip and going with 36 days between runs keeping him fresh — though winless in his last five starts, that persistent top-eight clustering is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for S R Bowring who is the lone confirmed front-runner and can secure an uncontested lead — won last time out over 7f (though on Soft) and has placed on Good; returning fresh at 48 days with Alistair Rawlinson in the plate, his style-fit tag applies to other shapes, not to the lead scenario where he is squarely in his role.
runners_data.comment: Back From Dubai won three starts back but has been unplaced on his latest outing, and at 48 days off the track his fitness is uncertain. Ranked ninth of ten on our figures, he faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Magic Lady Mae
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's three-year-old is just 11 days since her last run and has a single place from seven starts — all on Tapeta or Soft, with only one start on Good-equivalent ground; the step to 7f on turf Good to Firm is a clear unknown and, as a natural rear-runner crammed into a congested section, a clear passage looks far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Mister McGregor
runners_data.note: M Mullineaux's four-year-old wearing blinkers/eye-shield has placed twice at 7f on Tapeta and holds a pair of decent recent efforts (3rd, 2nd); Kieran O'Neill takes the ride and while the horse has tactical ability, his natural hold-up style is being mapped forward against his instincts and sim-going returns (0W1P) are modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mister McGregor faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and that third and second in recent starts offer a sliver of hope, but he's hard to fancy at these weights from stall six.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine rivals to push him, he can ease into a lead and control tempo from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up horses — Donald, Wilde And Dandy, Groundsman, Sir David, Barbuda Bay, Magic Lady Mae and Mister McGregor are all natural hold-up types, with Von Trotter and Sprinting Speed sharing similar closer profiles — meaning the pace behind the leader will be modest and the midfield is likely to be congested. With Back From Dubai able to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop, the race sets up as a front-runner's paradise: he can control fractions, steal a march at the top of the straight, and the hold-up horses face a searching closing test to reel him in on a flat, galloping track that rewards front-runners running in their role. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or lead-tracking profile; true closers must generate their own momentum through a tightly bunched pack, which is an inherently low-probability outcome given how few horses will be genuinely up with the pace. The field holds far more hold-up types than the race map can place authentically at the rear — Barbuda Bay, Wilde And Dandy, Groundsman, Magic Lady Mae and Mister McGregor are all likely to be pushed further forward than ideal but Back From Dubai is best placed to secure the true lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Back From Dubai Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai leads unchallenged and sets a controlled, honest-but-not-frenetic pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai can coast along the rail at Doncaster, use the flat straight to his advantage, and the compact hold-up pack behind him faces maximum ground to make up; a horse who won last time on soft over 7f and is returning fresh (48 days) has the profile to last home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the congested hold-up pack swarms over a stopping leader.
scenarios.body: A modest tempo can create a false race where the hold-up horses sweep through in a bunched finish, with those best suited to 7f on Good to Firm ground peeling widest to find clean air.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Raider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed midfield horses secures a prominent berth and tracks Back From Dubai before striking decisively.
scenarios.body: A horse such as Barbuda Bay or Von Trotter, if able to sit just off the pace at the top of the straight, could pounce before the true hold-up horses arrive; the flat Doncaster track rewards the well-positioned traveller.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sole Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If pace proves genuinely fast enough to set up a race for a single late finisher who threads through cleanly.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape given there is only one confirmed front-runner and the tempo is expected to be sustainable rather than suicidal; only a significant miscalculation of fractions would generate enough daylight for a genuine late closer.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai — if Alistair Rawlinson slides across to the rail unchallenged in the first furlong and settles into a rhythm, this race could be over a long way from home; watch for any rival willing to press him early as that is the single biggest threat to his dominance.

Congestion in the hold-up pack — with seven or eight horses all seeking a rear-to-midfield position and only one genuine pace-setter, the opening quarter-mile could see significant scrimmaging and traffic issues; runners on the outside (Wilde And Dandy, Groundsman) may be best placed to avoid trouble.

Von Trotter's position — if Oliver Stammers pushes forward to track Back From Dubai immediately, Von Trotter becomes a serious danger as the natural pace companion and could inherit the lead if the front-runner ties up late; watch the early positional battle between these two.

Barbuda Bay's layoff — 49 days off for Roger Teal's three-year-old is notable and, combined with a fade-in-finish flag and hold-up style, this horse needs everything to go right; monitor paddock condition and how quickly Dougie Costello slots him into position.

Going correction — the race card states Good but all going reports confirm Good to Firm throughout the card at Doncaster; any horse whose form notes show a preference for softer conditions (Back From Dubai's win came on Soft) should be assessed with the firmer surface in mind.

races.name: Grace And Dotty Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist with solid recent placed form at 6f on good ground (W5P record at similar going), trained by Gemma Tutty and ridden by Oliver Stammers; needs the pace to be genuine to get into contention from the rear, which is a risk with only one front-runner.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a second three starts back, Mark's Choice has been knocking on the door in recent starts — distance and going experience tick, 26 days since his last run suggests he's fresh, and he draws stall one. The risk is he's yet to win in his last five.

runners_data.name: Shazani
runners_data.note: Bowring-trained hold-up type whose going figures at this trip are modest (0W2P on similar), and the redistribution to midfield means it is unlikely to get its natural position at the back; the style mismatch and weak course-distance form suppress its chance regardless of scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Shazani has placed in each of his last two starts — third last time out and second two starts back — yet remains yet to win in recent starts, and his 36-day absence gives slight pause; experience over today's trip and going at least ensures he won't be inconvenienced by conditions.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: O'Meara's three-year-old has winning form at 6f on good ground and arrives on an 11-day turnaround with David Nolan aboard; true running style is hold-up but it's the most capable of the redistributed trio of finding a competitive midfield position, and its recent form figures (4-1-2) give it genuine each-way interest.|
runners_data.comment: Come On Over showed well when winning two starts back, but a fourth last time out tempers expectations; he has run over today's distance and going, and 131 lb is a stiff enough ask for a horse rated 68.

runners_data.name: Ay Gee Ell
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained four-year-old whose recent history is dominated by 5f runs on going softer than today, with no wins or places on similar going; double headgear fitted but form figures (3-0-4-8-9-9) give little encouragement, and running out of its natural hold-up role compounds the negatives.|
runners_data.comment: Ay Gee Ell showed promise with a third six starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, while our rating of 73 puts him ahead of his official mark; the concern is a trainer operating at just 2% in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: Knight's consistent three-year-old carries a strong profile — 1W4P from recent 6f and 7f runs on good and standard ground — and her prominent style means she is ideally positioned to track the leader and challenge in the final furlong; Neil Callan's experience is a positive in a tactical race like this.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Startled Lady faces a stiff ask, though she does bring last-time-out winning form and experience over today's trip and going. The 130 lb burden from stall two makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: Camacho's three-year-old has a solid placed record at sprint trips and is a natural prominent runner suited to tracking Ziggy's Condor; limited form at Doncaster specifically and only one similar-going run in the sample (0W1P) leaves a slight unknown, but the style profile is perfectly aligned with the expected race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts despite a pair of runner-up finishes, Celtic Arrow has hit the frame but struggles to convert; ranked seventh of eight on our figures, she faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and arrives reasonably fresh at 31 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Tinkler's seven-year-old has shown solid placed form at 6f on good ground (1W3P similar going) but carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish, which is a critical concern when asking it to close from off the pace in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo; the 3lb claimer Alex Jary adds a slight query.|
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last three completed starts, Another Investment arrives here in decent nick after a 28-day break, with experience over today's distance and going in his favour. Winless in recent starts, but his placed efforts give him solid claims off 137 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby-trained five-year-old running just three days after its last start with a hood fitted; races prominently but is mapped as the sole genuine front-runner, and while that gives it tactical control, the quick turnaround and a form string reading 2-6-4-5-0-U raises durability concerns — it may set the shape without being able to finish it.|
runners_data.comment: Ziggy's Condor holds the highest rating in the field and owns a solid speed figure, with experience over today's distance and going in his favour from stall three — the main concern is that he unseated last time out and remains winless in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Ziggy's Condor is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f Doncaster handicap and, racing just three days after its last run with headgear fitted, is likely to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a sustainable rather than scorching gallop on good-to-firm ground. Startled Lady and Celtic Arrow will press forward into prominent positions just off the leader, creating a compact, controlled pace scenario that favours those able to travel smoothly in the first two or three lengths of the pace. The hold-up horses — Mark's Choice, Another Investment, Shazani, Come On Over, and Ay Gee Ell — will be hunting from the rear, but with only one genuine pace-setter dictating a measured tempo, the race is unlikely to generate the strong early fractions that allow true closers to cut through. This shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track Ziggy's Condor at close range and quicken from a good position entering the final two furlongs. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically get their natural positions: Shazani, Come On Over, and Ay Gee Ell are all redistributed to midfield on the map, but Startled Lady and Celtic Arrow are most likely to secure the genuine prominent slots behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor sets a measured pace and the prominent pair track comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Ziggy's Condor dictates from the front unchallenged, and Startled Lady or Celtic Arrow, travelling within themselves in second or third, have enough fuel to pounce in the final furlong on ground that rewards those who conserve energy early. This is the dominant shape in a race with a lone front-runner and a cluster of prominent types positioned ideally to exploit a sustainable tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor goes too fast early given its quick turnaround and fades, opening the door for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: A quicker-than-expected gallop from Ziggy's Condor, possibly exacerbated by its 3-day freshness and blinkers, sets up a legitimate closing run for the hold-up brigade in the final furlong. Mark's Choice, with strong recent form at the trip on similar going, and Another Investment, who shows consistent placed form at 6f on good ground, are the logical beneficiaries if the pace burns itself out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at an even tempo and the redistributed hold-up horses manage to secure better-than-expected positions near the pace.
scenarios.body: Come On Over, who has recent winning form at the trip on good ground, is the most likely of the redistributed trio to find a prominent position in running given its course and distance profile and in-form jockey booking. Shazani lacks the form profile at this trip on this going to capitalise even if the shape partially suits, making Come On Over the standout chance in this secondary scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor has a blow-up race given the quick return and the race devolves into a sprint from the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With the sole pace-setter dropping out catastrophically, positions become meaningless and the race is won on raw speed in the final 1f, which plays into Startled Lady's consistent placed form at this trip. Another Investment's placed record on similar going makes it relevant here, though its documented tendency to fade late is a genuine concern even in a collapsed-pace scenario.

watchPoints.text: Ziggy's Condor's 3-day turnaround is the pivotal risk factor — if it blows up or fades sharply after setting the pace, the entire dominant scenario unravels and hold-up types like Mark's Choice gain significantly.|

Startled Lady's prominent style and strong placed record make her the most naturally-suited horse to this race shape, but watch whether Neil Callan can secure a position directly behind Ziggy's Condor before Celtic Arrow does — track position at the 4f mark will be decisive.|

Come On Over has the best form of the redistributed hold-up trio and David Nolan may ride it more aggressively than its natural style suggests — watch for it to be ridden closer to the pace than expected, which would upgrade its chance considerably.|

Another Investment's documented fading tendency in the finish is particularly relevant on a day when the going is good-to-firm at Doncaster — fast ground often exposes stamina limitations at 6f for hold-up horses asked to finish strongly, and its prominent OR of 70 may flatter its current ability to see it out.|

Celtic Arrow has raced predominantly on standard and softer surfaces in its short career (only 1 run on similar going); watch whether the quicker-than-usual conditions at Doncaster today present a question that its form doesn't fully answer.|
